stories.headline: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Secretly Inflated Advertising Prices
stories.summary:
The Federal Trade Commission and a bipartisan coalition of 22 states filed a lawsuit Monday against Amazon, alleging the e-commerce giant secretly inflated advertising prices paid by more than 1.2 million sellers and brands over the past seven years. The complaint, filed in the Western District of Washington, alleges Amazon imposed hidden surcharges that resulted in advertisers being overcharged by tens of billions of dollars. Amazon denied the claims.

The suit represents one of the most significant antitrust actions against Amazon to date and follows earlier FTC litigation targeting the company's retail marketplace practices. The bipartisan nature of the state coalition — spanning both Republican- and Democratic-led states — signals broad political appetite for reining in Amazon's advertising business, which has grown into one of the largest in the world behind Google and Meta.

Amazon's advertising segment generates more than $50 billion annually and has become a central profit driver for the company. Regulators argue the alleged hidden surcharges distorted competition and harmed small businesses that depend on Amazon's platform to reach customers. The company maintains its advertising products are fairly priced and competitive.

The case adds to a growing wave of federal and state antitrust enforcement targeting major technology platforms. A ruling against Amazon could reshape how the company prices and discloses advertising fees, with potential ripple effects across the broader digital advertising industry.

stories.headline: Update: Trump Presses Apple to Rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' After Google Complies
stories.summary:
President Trump has personally contacted Apple to request the company rename Lake Ontario as 'Lake America' on its Maps platform, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum confirmed Monday. Burgum said Trump reached out to Apple directly and indicated the change was likely imminent. Google updated its maps over the weekend, displaying 'Lake America' for U.S.-based users while retaining 'Lake Ontario' for Canadian users and showing both names internationally.

Trump signed an executive order last week directing the renaming of Lake Ontario, framing it as a response to the breakdown of U.S.-Canada trade negotiations. The order directs Burgum to update the Geographic Names Information System, the official U.S. government database. Not all platforms are complying: MapQuest publicly refused the change, gained top placement on the Canadian App Store as a result, and released a tool letting users rename the lake themselves.

The renaming has provoked a sharp backlash in Canada. Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a lakeside sign reading 'Lake Ontario Now and Always' in English and French, declaring the lake's name would not change regardless of U.S. directives. Several Ontario-based utilities and agencies briefly displayed the 'Lake America' label due to third-party mapping services, then apologized and said they were working to restore the original name.

The episode has become a flashpoint in the broader and deteriorating U.S.-Canada relationship, with the trade war generating economic friction on both sides of the border. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday accused Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney of walking away from a trade deal for domestic political reasons, a charge Carney's government has rejected.

stories.headline: Bessent Meets Russian Finance Minister at G20, Signaling U.S. Openness to Engagement with Moscow
stories.summary:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met Monday with Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Asheville, North Carolina, the Russian government confirmed. The meeting marks the first time Russia's top financial official has attended a G20 gathering in person since Moscow's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and represents a notable step toward high-level economic engagement between Washington and Moscow.

The encounter underscored a sharp divergence between the United States and its European allies over how to treat Russia diplomatically and economically. European governments, which have pursued coordinated sanctions and sought to isolate Moscow in international forums, have watched the Trump administration's warming posture toward Russia with growing alarm. Bessent's meeting with Siluanov came on the same day he opened the G20 with a vow of more Iran sanctions, reflecting the administration's selective approach to financial pressure.

The Trump administration has signaled broader interest in restarting dialogue with Russia, including through Driscoll's earlier involvement in back-channel discussions aimed at ending the war in Ukraine. Critics, including many European officials and U.S. Democrats, argue that engaging Russia at venues like the G20 legitimizes an aggressor and undermines the sanctions architecture built since 2022. Supporters of the approach contend diplomatic engagement is necessary to eventually negotiate a settlement in Ukraine.

The Bessent-Siluanov meeting had not been publicly announced in advance and was disclosed by the Russian government. The U.S. Treasury Department had not issued a public statement on the meeting as of Monday.

stories.headline: Update: House Returns from Recess with Government Shutdown Vote as Top Priority
stories.summary:
The U.S. House of Representatives returned Monday from a five-week August recess with lawmakers facing a critical vote on a stopgap spending bill to keep the federal government funded through early December. The measure is designed to avert a shutdown before the November midterm elections, now nine weeks away. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) spoke with reporters as Democrats sought to frame the week's agenda ahead of an election in which they are trying to retake the chamber.

Lawmakers are also expected to vote on a resolution condemning socialism and on a motion to censure Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards. The compressed legislative calendar reflects the intense pressure both parties face heading into midterms, with control of the House and Senate both in play.

The return to Washington comes amid a turbulent backdrop: renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities, rising gas prices, expiring Affordable Care Act subsidies that have pushed up insurance costs, and a series of senior White House staff departures. Rep. James Clyburn (D-S.C.) told NBC's Meet the Press that if Democrats retake the House, they should focus on affordability rather than pursuing impeachment proceedings against President Trump.

Republicans argue they have delivered on economic and border security priorities and that the spending bill reflects fiscal responsibility. Democrats counter that the administration's tariff and foreign policy decisions have created economic instability that demands a change in congressional leadership.

stories.headline: Update: Bessent Opens G20 Meeting in Asheville, Vows More Iran Sanctions Within Weeks
stories.summary:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent opened the Group of 20 finance ministers summit in Asheville, North Carolina, on Monday under significant strain, with U.S. allies skeptical of American leadership following aggressive tariffs on major trading partners and a six-month war with Iran that has kept global energy prices elevated. Bessent told reporters he believes the Iranian economy could be brought to its knees "within weeks or months" through sustained financial pressure, and announced plans to sanction an additional Iranian bank as part of what the administration calls "Operation Economic Outcast."

Bessent said the European Union had offered "fulsome support" for the U.S. sanctions campaign, and the EU issued a statement welcoming additional economic pressure on Iran. France's finance minister said he hopes the G20 will produce an agreed statement on economic growth but acknowledged global conditions are "a bit like the weather in Asheville — unpredictable and foggy."

Diplomats and former officials cautioned that the U.S. may struggle to build a unified coalition given its strained relationships with allies over tariffs. Daniel Fried, a former assistant secretary of state under President George W. Bush, said Washington would need to show greater care in consulting with partners than it has in recent months if it wants meaningful international backing on Iran.

The G20 summit comes days after the U.S. and Iran exchanged fresh strikes, including a U.S. attack on rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz. The simultaneous diplomatic and military tracks reflect the administration's strategy of combining economic pressure with targeted military action, though no clear exit strategy has emerged.

stories.headline: Trump Warns Communities Against Rejecting AI Data Centers, Wading Into Midterm Flash Point
stories.summary:
President Trump on Monday issued a sharp warning to communities pushing back against artificial intelligence data centers, writing on Truth Social that localities rejecting the infrastructure risk becoming "backwards and poor." The statement represents a significant escalation of the administration's commitment to the AI build-out, entering a politically charged fight that Republican candidates in many districts have been trying to avoid just nine weeks before midterm elections.

A recent poll found that three-quarters of Americans oppose having data centers built near their homes, citing concerns about electricity and water consumption. The backlash has become a tangible issue in local and state races across the country, with residents and officials in communities from the Pacific Northwest to the Mid-Atlantic raising objections to the scale of resource use involved in large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Trump framed the issue as a matter of national competitiveness, arguing that blocking data centers cedes ground to China in the global race for AI dominance. Supporters of data center expansion point to examples such as Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft's facilities funded a new high school, hospital, and aquatic center, arguing the economic benefits outweigh the costs.

Critics counter that the administration is prioritizing the interests of large technology investors over the concerns of local residents dealing with strained power grids and water supplies. The political dynamics are complicated: some Democrats who might otherwise oppose the projects have supported AI investment as an economic development tool, while some Republicans in affected districts have been reluctant to embrace the president's position.

stories.headline: Update: U.S. and Iran Exchange Strikes for First Time Since July; Trump Vows Response
stories.summary:
The United States and Iran traded military strikes for the first time in more than a month after U.S. Central Command hit Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, saying the launchers were positioned to deploy sea mines into the critical shipping waterway. The strike killed two people and wounded two others, according to officials. Iran retaliated by launching ballistic missiles and drones at U.S. military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, though American forces intercepted the incoming fire with no reported U.S. casualties.

President Trump vowed further action Monday, telling Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst, 'We're going to hit them hard. There will be a response.' The renewed exchange marks a significant escalation after a roughly five-week lull following Trump's pause of a two-week U.S. military campaign in late July. The attack on Larak Island was the first known U.S. strike on Iranian territory since that pause.

The flare-up comes just days after the administration announced 'Operation Economic Outcast,' a Treasury-led effort to cut Iran off from the global financial system, signaling a strategic shift toward economic rather than military pressure. The latest strikes suggest that approach has not halted hostilities. Four generals and admirals had reportedly advised against prolonging the war, according to the Washington Post, though Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell disputed the framing of that report, saying formal 'non-concurs' from commanders are standard procedure.

The conflict, now past its six-month mark, has rattled energy markets and strained U.S. alliances in the Middle East. Iran's missiles toward Jordan — a U.S. ally — were intercepted, but the targeting of Jordanian and UAE bases underscores Iran's willingness to widen the geographic scope of the conflict. Congress returns from recess Monday with government funding legislation as its immediate priority, adding domestic political pressure to the administration's wartime management.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi Announces Retirement from Argentina International Football
stories.summary:
Lionel Messi announced Monday that he is retiring from international football, ending a 21-year career with Argentina that included the 2022 World Cup title and two Copa America championships. The 39-year-old, who scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina — both all-time national records — said in a statement that 'the time has come' and that he has 'nothing left to give' the national side. He confirmed the decision was made July 21, two days after Argentina lost to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final, and said the recent death of his father Jorge deepened his conviction to step away.

Messi scored eight goals and four assists across the 2026 World Cup tournament, finishing as one of the competition's leading contributors despite the final-round defeat. He is the second-highest scorer in World Cup history with 21 goals, trailing only France's Kylian Mbappé. His retirement from international duty does not end his club career; Messi remains under contract with MLS side Inter Miami through the end of the 2028 season.

The announcement closes what is widely regarded as one of the greatest international careers in the sport's history. Messi had previously retired from Argentina duty in 2016 after a Copa America final loss before reversing course. This time, he indicated the decision is final, writing: 'I'm leaving with the peace of mind and pride of having given you, together with my teammates, moments' of lasting significance.

The retirement carries particular resonance in Argentina, where Messi's 2022 World Cup victory ended decades of near-misses and elevated him to near-mythological status. His continued presence in MLS means American fans will retain access to arguably the sport's most decorated player, even as his chapter with the national team formally concludes.

stories.headline: DOT Shuts Down 110 Commercial Truck-Driving Schools Over English Proficiency Violations
stories.summary:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced Monday the emergency shutdown of more than 110 commercial truck-driving schools, accusing them of certifying over 5,000 drivers who had failed federally mandated English language proficiency tests. The Department of Transportation said the schools willfully disregarded long-standing federal rules requiring commercial drivers to be able to communicate in English during roadside interactions with law enforcement and in emergency situations. The action was coordinated with the Department of Homeland Security and other agencies as part of a broader administration crackdown on fraud in the trucking industry.

Federal regulations have required commercial truck drivers operating in the United States to demonstrate English language proficiency for decades, on the grounds that the ability to communicate with inspectors, read road signs, and respond to emergencies is a safety necessity. Duffy said the more than 5,000 drivers trained at the shuttered schools had been cited for English proficiency violations during roadside inspections, indicating the licenses were being issued without adequate testing.

Supporters of the crackdown, primarily Republican officials and transportation safety advocates, argue the rule exists to protect public safety on highways and that schools circumventing it posed a direct risk to other motorists. Critics, including immigration and labor advocates, are likely to frame the action as part of the administration's broader immigration enforcement posture, given that English proficiency rules disproportionately affect foreign-born drivers. The administration has not detailed what happens to the more than 5,000 drivers whose certifications are now in question.

The announcement was made from Detroit alongside DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin as part of a multi-agency effort the administration has framed as targeting systemic fraud. The trucking industry is a critical backbone of U.S. supply chains, and the scale of the shutdown — more than 110 schools simultaneously — represents one of the most sweeping federal actions against commercial driver training providers in recent memory.

stories.headline: Met Museum Cancels John Galliano Exhibition After Backlash Over Antisemitic Past
stories.summary:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York has cancelled a major retrospective exhibition honoring fashion designer John Galliano after widespread criticism tied to his 2011 conviction for making antisemitic and racist remarks. The exhibition, titled 'John Galliano: Horizons,' had been scheduled to open in May 2027 and would have served as the theme for the next Met Gala, which was set to coincide with Yom HaShoah — Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day — on May 3. Galliano announced the cancellation Monday, saying 'after much reflection and discussion with the Met,' he concluded it was best for the exhibition not to take place.

Galliano was fired as creative director of Dior in 2011 after being caught on video making statements in a Paris bar in which he declared admiration for Adolf Hitler and directed antisemitic and racist insults at other patrons. A French court found him guilty of abuse. He subsequently underwent treatment for addiction and alcoholism and has publicly expressed remorse on multiple occasions, noting in Monday's statement '15 years of sobriety and recovery' and saying he 'remains fully accountable for the pain caused.'

New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who had lobbied the Met against the exhibition, called the decision correct, saying it had been 'a gut punch to the Jewish community' at 'a rising time of antisemitism.' The Anti-Defamation League also expressed support for the cancellation. Vogue global editorial director Anna Wintour, a Met trustee and Met Gala co-chair, backed Galliano, calling his decision to cancel 'very courageous and a measure of the man he is.'

The cancellation raises broader questions about the boundaries of institutional rehabilitation for public figures convicted of hate-related offenses and about the responsibilities of major cultural institutions in adjudicating those boundaries. It also disrupts planning for the 2026 Met Gala, one of the most prominent annual events in the global fashion calendar, which will now require a new creative theme.

stories.headline: Update: Ferry Death Toll Rises to Eight with 18 Still Missing Off Northern Cyprus
stories.summary:
Rescue operations continued Monday off the coast of northern Cyprus after a passenger ferry capsized Sunday, with eight confirmed dead and 18 passengers still unaccounted for. The vessel, carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members, began taking on water shortly after departing the coastal town of Kyrenia en route to Tasucu, Turkey. The ship has fully sunk and lies at a depth of 514 meters, complicating search efforts.

The captain, seven crew members, and another man were arrested Monday as authorities sought to determine the cause of the disaster. The prime minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus said the vessel was struck by two waves in succession, the second of which caused it to take on water before capsizing. A three-day period of national mourning was declared.

The human toll was underscored by accounts from survivors, including a mother who described losing her grip on her 12-year-old daughter as the child slipped from her hands in engine oil-slicked water. Nineteen people were being treated in hospitals, with conditions ranging from minor to severe. Authorities are working to recover the vessel's black box to establish a full account of events.

This incident represents a significant maritime disaster in a region where such accidents are uncommon. The privately owned Filo Jet vessel sails under the Turkish flag and was operated by Filo Denizcilik, which expressed condolences. The TRNC, recognized only by Turkey, controls the northern third of Cyprus following the island's division in 1974.

stories.headline: Unification Church Leader Sentenced to Two Years for Bribing South Korea's Former First Lady
stories.summary:
Han Hak-ja, the 83-year-old leader of the Unification Church, was sentenced to two years in prison Monday after a South Korean court found her church guilty of bribing former first lady Kim Keon Hee and committing other political funding offences. The court determined the church gave Kim two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, collectively worth approximately $57,900, between April and July 2022 in exchange for business and political favors. Prosecutors released photos of $19 million in cash found in Han's personal safe.

Kim, the wife of impeached and ousted President Yoon Suk Yeol, was herself sentenced to 20 months in prison earlier this year for accepting the bribes. She admitted to receiving the luxury goods but claimed she returned them without using them. Prosecutors described the case as the first time authorities have formally confirmed the church's attempts to purchase political influence in South Korea.

Han, the widow of church founder Sun Myung Moon, had repeatedly denied the allegations. The Unification Church — formally known as The Family Federation for World Peace and Unification — was founded in South Korea in the 1950s and is recognized globally for its mass wedding ceremonies. Critics have long described the organization as cult-like and accused it of coercing members into large financial donations.

The case has broad international dimensions. The church's ties to politics in South Korea, Japan, and the United States have come under scrutiny in recent years, particularly following the 2022 assassination of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, whose alleged killer blamed the church for financially ruining his family. The church has been ordered to dissolve in Japan and is banned in several other countries.

stories.headline: Pakistan Says Six to Seven Muslim Nations Seeking to Join New Defense Pact as U.S.-Iran Conflict Continues
stories.summary:
Pakistan announced Monday that six to seven Muslim-majority countries have expressed interest in joining the Mecca Defense Agreement, a security and military cooperation framework, as top diplomats from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey convened in Istanbul to discuss the pact's expansion. The meeting comes amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, which has elevated regional security concerns across the Middle East and South Asia.

The gathering signals a potential reshaping of Muslim-world security architecture at a moment of significant geopolitical stress. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey — three of the most militarily capable majority-Muslim nations — are testing the practical substance of the agreement and its capacity to attract broader membership. The identities of the interested nations were not disclosed.

The talks carry particular significance given the six-month duration of U.S.-Iran hostilities, which have created pressure on regional powers to define their strategic alignments. A formalized Muslim defense bloc, if it develops further, could complicate existing alliance structures involving NATO members Turkey and other U.S. partners in the region.

Bloomberg and Al Jazeera reported on the Istanbul meeting, which represents one of the more concrete multilateral security developments to emerge from the instability generated by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. Details on the agreement's mutual defense obligations and command structures were not publicly released.

stories.headline: Update: Suspect Arrested in Swiss Rave Shooting That Killed Italian Woman, 22
stories.summary:
Swiss police arrested a 43-year-old Swiss man early Monday in connection with the fatal shooting at a techno rave in Aarau, Switzerland, ending a nearly 24-hour manhunt. Maria Spinelli, a 22-year-old Italian national, was killed at the event held at a horse racing track, and five others aged 24 to 27 were hospitalized with injuries ranging from minor to severe. Authorities said they are operating under the assumption that the perpetrator acted alone.

The shooting occurred at approximately 2:30 a.m. Sunday at the Schachen race track, which had drawn an expected crowd of around 3,500 attendees. Aarau police had initially said they had no leads on the perpetrator and were uncertain whether a single individual or multiple people were responsible. The arrest marked a swift resolution to the manhunt, which had drawn cross-border support from German police.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni had previously expressed confidence that Swiss authorities would identify those responsible, and Italy's foreign ministry dispatched officials to Zurich to follow the investigation. The victim's Italian nationality added a diplomatic dimension to what is an otherwise rare instance of gun violence in Switzerland, a country with one of Europe's highest rates of gun ownership but comparatively few shooting incidents.

The last major shooting in Switzerland occurred in 2001, when a gunman killed 14 members of the regional parliament of Zug before taking his own life. Swiss authorities tightened firearms regulations in subsequent years. The motive in the Aarau case remains under investigation.

stories.headline: Update: Maduro Posts First Prison Photos Eight Months After U.S. Capture, Days After Venezuela Oil Deal
stories.summary:
Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro appeared in photos posted to his social media accounts Sunday, offering the first known images of him inside the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn since his capture by U.S. forces in Caracas in January. Maduro, who faces federal drug trafficking charges, wore a gray sweatsuit and appeared noticeably thinner, flashing peace signs and offering reassurances to supporters that he and his wife Cilia Flores — also in U.S. custody on related charges — remain "firm" and "serene."

The photos carry timestamps indicating they were taken June 25, one day after two major earthquakes killed more than 6,500 people in northern Venezuela, though they were posted Sunday — two days after President Trump announced what he called a breakthrough U.S.-Venezuela deal granting American majority control over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves. The timing of the release has drawn attention given the diplomatic significance of the oil agreement.

The Venezuela oil deal and Maduro's continued detention represent a major shift in U.S.-Venezuela relations. Supporters of the Trump administration argue the deal secures vital energy resources at a moment when the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict has driven up fuel prices. Critics and Maduro allies contend the arrangement is coercive and exploits Venezuela's political instability to extract its national resources.

Maduro has been held for eight months without trial as legal proceedings advance in the Southern District of New York. His detention, engineered through a military operation on Venezuelan soil, remains one of the most consequential and contested foreign-policy actions of the Trump administration's second term.

stories.headline: Modi and Putin Meet at Summit Promoting Multipolar World as Trump Tariffs Complicate India-Russia Ties
stories.summary:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at a two-day summit aimed at reinforcing a vision of a multipolar global order and expanding bilateral trade, even as U.S. tariff pressure tests India's longstanding policy of strategic autonomy. The summit, attended by leaders from multiple nations, is not officially anti-Western but has been used by Russian and Chinese officials to amplify an alternative to U.S.-led international institutions.

India's balancing act between Washington and Moscow has grown more difficult since Trump's return to the White House. U.S. tariffs have placed economic strain on Indian exports, while India continues to purchase discounted Russian oil — a practice that has drawn scrutiny from American officials seeking to tighten pressure on Moscow over Ukraine.

The meeting comes at a delicate moment in global geopolitics, with the U.S.-Iran conflict reshaping energy markets, the war in Ukraine entering a prolonged phase, and the Trump administration pursuing an assertive unilateral trade posture that has strained alliances worldwide. India's continued engagement with Russia provides Moscow a degree of diplomatic legitimacy it has struggled to maintain elsewhere.

Analysts note that India's position reflects a broader trend among major emerging economies seeking to avoid alignment with either Washington or its rivals. Modi has framed India's approach as principled nonalignment rather than defiance of the West, but the optics of a Modi-Putin summit — amid the Ukraine war and U.S. sanctions pressure — remain diplomatically sensitive.

stories.headline: Ukraine Aid Under Scrutiny as Corruption Investigations Reach Zelenskyy's Inner Circle
stories.summary:
The Biden- and Trump-era commitment of roughly $195 billion in total U.S. appropriations for Ukraine-related operations is facing renewed congressional and public scrutiny as corruption investigations have reached senior officials within President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's presidential office. Zelenskyy dismissed Iryna Mudra, a deputy head of his office, on Aug. 19 as anti-corruption investigators pursued a separate money-laundering case involving another senior official in the same office. Investigators have not named Mudra as a suspect.

Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Carrie Filipetti, now with the Vandenberg Coalition, told Fox News Digital that over 24 federal agencies are involved in oversight of U.S. military and economic aid, and that safeguards on the American side are robust. "A lot more work needs to be done," she acknowledged, "but we know, at least on the U.S. side, as we're providing support for their military, we have a lot of mechanisms."

Critics of ongoing U.S. aid, predominantly on the right, argue that the corruption cases demonstrate systemic institutional weakness in Ukraine and raise questions about accountability for taxpayer funds. Supporters of continued assistance counter that Ukraine's independent anti-corruption bodies are actively pursuing these cases — a sign of institutional functioning rather than failure — and that halting aid would benefit Russia far more than any internal Ukrainian misconduct.

The U.S. committed $67.8 billion in defense articles and services through March 2026 alone. With the war now in its fifth year and no clear diplomatic resolution in sight, the corruption disclosures add domestic political pressure at a moment when U.S. support for Ukraine is already a contested issue heading into the November midterms.

stories.headline: Dolly Parton Laid to Rest in Nashville Alongside Late Husband Carl Dean
stories.summary:
Country music legend Dolly Parton was buried Friday at Woodlawn Memorial Park and Mausoleum in Nashville, Tennessee, following a private family funeral, her great-niece Lainey Parton confirmed Saturday in an emotional social media tribute. Parton, who died earlier in the week at age 80, was interred beside her late husband Carl Dean. A brass plaque bearing both their names and engravings of their childhood homes marks the tomb.

Lainey Parton wrote: "It still doesn't feel real that she's gone. I'm going to miss her voice, her laugh, her hugs, and just knowing she was there." The family has asked that in lieu of flowers, donations be directed to Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, the program Parton founded to send free books to young children, which has mailed more than 300 million books since its inception.

A tribute concert was held Saturday at Nashville's Grand Ole Opry House, where Parton's niece Jada Star performed a song she recorded with her aunt in 2024. Country star Jelly Roll made a surprise appearance at the event. The Opry, regarded as the home of American country music, served as a fitting venue to honor a performer whose seven-decade career helped define the genre.

Parton, who was 46 when she launched the Imagination Library in honor of her illiterate father, leaves behind one of the most celebrated legacies in American popular music. Her death at 80 closes a chapter that spanned generations of artists and fans across the country.
